This ensures that only the front-most entry point into a non-empty region is processed [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the notes and passages that the technique involves discarding fragments that are 'not at the minimum depth value' and that this process is used to 'compute the start and end positions for the ray'. In ray marching, the 'minimum depth value' corresponds to the front-most intersection (entry point) with the bounding geometry. By discarding anything else, the system ensures that only the front-most entry point is used to define the start of the ray march into the volume, effectively skipping empty space and ensuring only the front-most entry is processed for the subsequent ray marching step.
